intro: A Hittite medical tablet (CTH 461) with graded prescriptions, each followed by a fallback 'if he does not get well from that': plant mixtures (cress, garlic, leek and other herbs) given for seven days to a patient ill 'inside' who will not eat; a treatment for limbs that are 'not well' using a sinew from an animal killed by a leopard; and treatments for a discharge from the penis. A colophon on the left edge names the scribe NU.GIŠKIRI₆, pupil of Ḫulanabi.

paras.en: [If …] inside … (innanaš šāt[ar]) […] … and he does not eat bread, he takes these herbs: seed of cress (ZÀ.AḪ.LI), … […] nuḫurtu (NU.LUḪ.ḪA) and a great deal(?) of AN.DAḪ.ŠUM-plant; and [ḫark]i- he takes in equal proportion(?), and [keeps giving] it to him for seven days. But a day passes in between (i.e. on alternate days?), (and) [he] keeps giving [it to him]. While he keeps giving him these herbs for seven days, he takes half (a measure?) of ḫarki-plant ('white plant'?) in exactly equal proportion(?). Then he voids(?) (iyai) and also lets (it) out downward(?), and [he …]

But if he does not get well from that, then he gives him wi[ne](?): he takes a bulb (gapanu) of garlic, a bulb of leek (GA.RAŠ), a bulb of šullittinni- (a vegetable), and he lets them in (to steep?), and [he sifts] them. He takes half (a measure?) of ḫarki-plant, and it with wine […], and [gives] it to him for seven days on an empty stomach(?); then he voids(?) and lets (it) out downward(?).

If he does not get well from that, […] he takes […], and they peel(?) it off, and he sifts(?) it in […], and he gives it to him to eat […] a bulb he gives in (it) […] gi[ves] (it) to him to eat […] šulli[ttinni- …] until he […] [break] […] … […] either … […] …apšiḫai- […] him … […] down … […] he treats(?) (him), and he […]

If a person's limbs are not well, then this […]: and while the pe[rson] does not see (it), he pours (it) on top into a hole; but the remedy […], and he takes away its root; he sews (it) into a leather cord (MATNU) (from an animal) which a leopard has killed. If … […] he takes, and they luššanu- it […], and they sprinkle it; then they ta[ke] it. But they take only the sinew of a ḫuitnaima- (wild animal?); he twists(?) (it) in, and he gets well. Days […]

[I]f (something) d[rips](?) from a person's penis, but it is not [se]men, then he heats a tappi- (compress?); […] he keeps placing (it) in(?) his penis, and it lies in (there) the whole night. As long as he

does not get well from that, he afterwards soaks(?) it (anda šuniyazzi) with this remedy. And if he is paššari- (circumcised?), then him […]; (if) he is not paššari-, then he presses the ḫapuri- (foreskin?) back, (and) … smears (it); then he draws the ḫapuri- forward. [He] gets well. And he keeps smearing it with lead alone.

And they strike it; and if it keeps getting larger(?) […] … […] … (kurušiyan) […] … Then quickly that one, once, dow[n …] … three times he presses (it) down. […] with a bronze implement […] … not […] … he gets well. A bed-cloth(?) (TÚG MAYALU) […]
[Colophon:] NU.GIŠKIRI₆ ('Gardener'), son of SAG(?), chief of the scribes, [pup]il of Ḫulanabi.
